data.body: WHAT: the 'Test before publishing' step (uv run pytest tests/ -q --timeout=420 -n auto, publish.yml verify job) took 5116 s (1:25:16): 12720 passed, 1 failed, 29 skipped on a ubuntu-latest runner (Python 3.12.3, xdist 3.8.0). Slower than the 1:17:46 in fix-ci-split-slow-tests. Not a duplicate: it adds that publish.yml's verify job also runs the full suite (a second copy of ci.yml's) and gates every publish on it; both fix-ci-split-slow-tests (split slow tests, budget, timeout-minutes) and fix-test-duration-profile (where the time goes) apply, and this should follow them: decide whether verify re-runs the full suite or reuses the ci.yml result for the same sha. NOT fixed here. ACCEPTANCE: verify's test step wall time reported before/after; budget from a workflow variable.

data.falsifier: pytest 9.1.1 on python 3.12.3 still exits 4 'file or directory not found' for '-- --co'
data.mechanism: 3.12.3 argparse handles '--' wrongly; pytest then runs collect-only: exit 5, 'no tests collected' (collect-only summary line), no 'not found' error
data.probe_output: collected 0 items; no tests collected in 0.00s; exit 5. Same pytest on 3.12.13: ERROR file or directory not found: --co, exit 4. In the repo on 3.12.3 it collected 7072 tests
data.question: Why does test_a_test_id_that_looks_like_an_option_is_not_one fail on the GitHub runner only?

evidence.note: CONFIRMED: python 3.12.3 + pytest 9.1.1 turns '-- --co' into collect-only (exit 5); 3.12.13 gives exit 4
ddflow brief --item run; no rule against env-scrubbing nested pytest
repro_facts.test_run checks the path, ./-prefixes dash ids, scrubs PYTEST_ADDOPTS/XDIST env; 3 regression tests fail on unfixed code, 16 pass in test_repro_bundle.py

data.rule: Do not use '--' to make a user-supplied value safe from an option parser: check it yourself and ./-prefix it. A test green on dev Python (3.12.13/3.13) can fail on the runner's 3.12.3.
data.title: Python 3.12.3 argparse breaks '--' for pytest: never rely on it to protect a dash-led argument
data.why: CI publish verify failed: 'pytest -- --co' ran collect-only (exit 5) on 3.12.3, exit 4 'not found' elsewhere.

chunk_findings.detail: `path_part = test_id.partition("::")[0].partition("[")[0]` truncates the file part at the first `[`, but a `[` before `::` can be part of a legal POSIX file path. For example, when `test_id` is `"test_x[0].py::test_ok"` and `test_x[0].py` exists, `path_part` becomes `"test_x"`. Since `where/test_x` does not exist, `test_run` returns exit_code=4 with “file or directory not found” instead of running the test. Parameterization appears after `::`, so the extra `[` split is unnecessary and creates a false negative for valid test files.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/repro_facts.py:test_run path_part

chunk_findings.detail: The filter removes only the exact key `"PYTEST_ADDOPTS"` (and exact-prefix `"PYTEST_XDIST_"`). On Windows, environment variable names are case-insensitive; a caller-set `pytest_addopts=--co` survives filtering, so the child pytest can still see `PYTEST_ADDOPTS` and exit 5 for the very case this change is meant to fix. The same case-sensitivity gap applies to mixed-case `PYTEST_XDIST_*` variables.

chunk_findings.detail: This still truncates the file part at the first `[` before `::`, and that is unnecessary after splitting at `::`. Concrete failure: cwd contains `test_x[0].py` with `def test_ok(): pass`; call `test_run(repo, "test_x[0].py::test_ok", ...)`. `path_part` becomes `"test_x"`, so `(Path(where) / path_part).exists()` is false and `test_run` returns exit_code=4 with “file or directory not found” even though the target file exists and the test should run. The new tests do not cover an existing path that has `[` before `::`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/repro_facts.py:test_run path_part = test_id.partition("::")[0].partition("[")[0]

chunk_findings.detail: The recorded command no longer matches what the new code does. For `test_id="--co"` with no such file, `test_run` does not invoke pytest and returns `exit_code=4`, but the `command` field is `pytest --tb=short -- --co` — the very command that on Python 3.12.3/pytest 9.1.1 gives exit 5/no tests collected. For an existing dash-led id it records `-- -test_x.py`, while the fixed execution uses `./-test_x.py` without `--`; either way the bundle records a command that does not reproduce the fact.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/repro_facts.py:test_run out = {"id": test_id, "command": "pytest --tb=short -- " + test_id}
